summary: Submitted draft/submission.json (action=check) with draft/check-plan-quorum.json and draft/check-harness-quorum.go: the consequence of the two-leader overlap, which the previous obligation recorded as its remaining question. No map change was needed, so the combined product carries only the new obligation and its check. The obligation c-committed-entry-stored-by-quorum states that an entry a node reports as committed at an index must be the entry a quorum of the voting configuration stores there, so a client write may not be acknowledged at a position where the other voters hold a different entry; it is registered on the existing commit-index fact through b-commit-advance (the commitment rule that produces the acknowledged index) and b-client-apply-verify (the contract that reports it), with b-follower-append-entries and b-elect-self as support, and bound by bind-commitment-recalculate at the commitment rule. The check reuses the overlap harness and extends it: after the transfer target becomes leader in the same term while the sitting leader is still in that term, the harness blocks both leader endpoints so neither can settle the term, waits for the initiating leader's transfer attempt to time out through its reloaded election interval so it accepts client work again, issues one client write, and then compares the acknowledged command and index against the only reachable voter's log entry and applied value at the same index. I verified the exact harness locally before it was moved into the draft: the test passes (exit 0) and shows the leader acknowledging the command at index 3 with its own log holding LogCommand data "from-d" and its FSM applying it, while the voter's log entry at index 3 is a LogNoop in the same term with no data, its applied value at that index is empty and its commit index has already reached 3. So the acknowledgement is backed by a quorum that does not hold the command, and the two logs carry different entries at one index and term. The plan records the fixed inputs, the binding, the oracle (the replica's data compared with the acknowledged command, with applicability requiring the same term so a lagging replica is never judged), the legality derivation from the commitment rule and the follower's term-only conflict handling, and the limits. Counterevidence and limits are explicit: under a single leadership the equal-index-equal-term assumption is sound, the voter's acknowledgement is honest about its own log position, the chain depends on the staged overlap and the block that keeps it alive, and only one index and one acknowledged write are observed without any client read or later recovery. Two mechanical notes are worth keeping: the first attempt was rejected because ReloadableConfig requires the election timeout to be at least the heartbeat timeout, which is why the harness waits through the leader's transfer timeout before writing, and the whole test now takes about eighteen seconds, well within the execution timeout. Optional preflight with the trusted validator returned valid=true; the next step would be the correspondence review of this measured comparison.
